slots.title: Are Plastic Bags Actually Recyclable? (2026)
slots.why: Novolex Holdings, Inteplast Group and Mettler Packaging, three of the biggest bag manufacturers in the country, which sold bags marketed as recyclable under California law and then could not show that recycling facilities were actually processing them. Four more producers had already settled the same claims months earlier.
slots.felt: She has a drawer or a bin stuffed with bags and she gets down on the kitchen floor to sort them, then carries them back to the grocery store bin, because she was raised not to waste and because she wants to leave the place better than she found it. Her back is not what it was. She wants to know the trip meant something.

slots.title: Are Store Brand Eye Drops Safe? What Got Pulled From Walgreens, CVS and Kroger (2026)
slots.why: K.C. Pharmaceuticals, Inc. of Pomona, California. It does not sell under its own name. It fills the bottles that carry the Walgreens, CVS, Kroger, Rite Aid, Equate, DG Health, TopCare, Good Sense, Leader, Good Neighbor Pharmacy, Harris Teeter, Publix, Meijer, H-E-B, Foster and Thrive and GeriCare labels. FDA put its sterility failures in writing in a 2023 warning letter and the firm recalled 397,430 bottles that same year. Three years later it recalled eight times that number for the same category of failure.
slots.felt: Her eyes started burning and blurring by mid afternoon somewhere around 48 and nobody warned her that dry eye arrives with everything else. The cheap store brand bottle lives in her purse and she uses it two or three times a day, straight onto the surface of her eye.

slots.title: Does Laminate Flooring Give Off Formaldehyde? (2026)
slots.why: Lumber Liquidators. After a 60 Minutes investigation aired on March 1, 2015, the company told investors in a regulatory filing that its Chinese-made laminate complied with California's formaldehyde emission limits. The California Air Resources Board had already informed the company in 2013 and 2014 that samples pulled from its own California stores failed formaldehyde testing.
slots.keyword: does laminate flooring off gas formaldehyde
slots.felt: She put that floor in herself, or paid to have it done, back when the house needed to look like she had it together. Now the windows stay shut from November to March and her eyes water and her throat is scratchy every winter, and she has been calling it allergies for ten years.

slots.title: Does Prevagen Actually Work? (2026)
slots.why: Quincy Bioscience. It put clinically shown to improve memory on the package starting around 2011 and took it to national television and radio in 2013, and kept the claim running through seven years of litigation. Internal company documents produced at trial showed the jellyfish protein is rapidly digested and unlikely to reach the brain at all.
slots.felt: She walks into the kitchen and cannot remember why. It happens three times a week now and nobody tells her anything except that it is just her age, so when she sees the box at the pharmacy counter promising her memory back she picks it up, because the alternative is being scared.

slots.title: Does Woolite Really Revive Your Colors? (2026)
slots.why: Reckitt Benckiser, which sold Woolite Gentle Cycle and Woolite Darks under the words "Color Renew" and "revives colors," charging for a promise that clothes would come out of the wash better than they went in. It paid millions rather than prove the claim.
slots.felt: She is not buying new clothes the way she used to. The good sweater and the black pants have to last, so she pays the extra couple of dollars for the gentle bottle with the promise on it, and then watches the black go grey anyway and quietly blames her washing machine or herself.

slots.title: Is Ultra Processed Food a Risk On Its Own, Separate From Calories? (2026)
slots.felt: She has counted calories, cut fat, cut sugar and cut salt across thirty years of being told each one was the answer. She has never been told the manufacturing itself might be the thing.
slots.study: European Heart Journal, May 2026. Luigina Guasti and colleagues, University of Insubria. A European Society of Cardiology clinical consensus statement.
slots.takeaway: It is not only what these foods contain. It is what being manufactured does to them, and that is now treated as a risk in its own right.

slots.title: Is A Keratin Treatment Safe? (2026)
slots.why: GIB, LLC, trading as Brazilian Blowout. The California Attorney General settled with them on January 30, 2012 for labelling the Acai Smoothing Solution and the Professional Smoothing Solution as formaldehyde free when both released formaldehyde gas as soon as heat hit them. They paid $600,000, half of it Proposition 65 civil penalties. The words on the bottle were the lie, not the fine print inside it.
slots.felt: The frizz got worse after forty-five and the humidity wins every single morning. Three hours in the chair and a treatment that costs more than her last pair of good shoes buys her twelve weeks of hair that behaves. She sat in that chair with her eyes watering and the stylist opened a window and neither of them said anything about it.

slots.title: Is Angry Orange Stain Remover Safe? What Was Growing in 1.5 Million Bottles (2026)
slots.why: Thrasio, the holding company that bought the Angry Orange brand. It kept the product on shelves at Walmart, Target, Home Depot, Meijer, Staples, TJ Maxx, Amazon, Chewy and its own site from March 2019 all the way through December 2025 before the recall landed.
slots.felt: The dog had an accident on the carpet again and she is down on her knees with the windows shut, spraying and scrubbing with her face maybe eighteen inches from the wet patch, breathing it the whole time.

slots.title: Is Antibacterial Hand Soap Safe? (2026)
slots.why: Henkel's Dial. When the FDA pulled triclosan off the market, Dial Complete reformulated with benzalkonium chloride, one of exactly three ingredients the FDA had just set aside because nobody had submitted the safety and effectiveness data, and kept the word Antibacterial on the front of the pump.
slots.felt: Her hands split at the knuckles every winter and bleed when she makes a fist, and she has been told it is her age and the dry air. She washes them thirty times a day at a sink where the pump promises to kill 99.99% of germs, and she has never once thought of that bottle as part of the problem.

The state had to make it do that.

slots.felt: She is watching brown patches come up on her cheeks and along her jaw and everybody tells her it is hormones and it is just her age. slots.title: Is Krud Kutter Really Non-Toxic? (2026)
slots.why: Rust-Oleum Corporation, which put "Non-Toxic" and "Earth Friendly" on the front of Krud Kutter cleaners for nine years, then agreed under a court-approved settlement to permanently strip "Non-Toxic" off the package and bury a qualifier behind an asterisk on "Earth Friendly" rather than defend the words at trial.
slots.felt: She reaches for the bottle that says non-toxic because her hands crack open every winter now and her chest gets tight after she scrubs the shower. She is not being fussy. She is 54 and her body reacts to things it never used to react to, and she picked that bottle specifically to be safe.

slots.title: Short Hard Workouts or Long Easy Ones: Which Does More for Your Heart? (2026)
slots.felt: She does not have an hour. She has been told an hour is what it takes, so she does nothing at all, and she feels bad about that on top of everything else.

slots.takeaway: The short version is not a lesser version. And whichever one you pick, the gains only last as long as you keep doing it.

slots.title: Is Redken Shampoo Safe? What L'Oreal Asked New York State For (2026)
slots.why: L'Oreal USA. New York capped 1,4-dioxane in personal care at 1 ppm. Instead of meeting it, L'Oreal USA applied to the state for waivers on 69 salon products and got them, listing Redken All Soft Shampoo at 4.5 ppm, Redken Color Extend Graydiant at 3.67 ppm, Kerastase Densifique Women Bain at 4.6 ppm, and L'Oreal Professionnel Serie Expert Volumetry at 7.23 ppm. That is seven times the legal limit, in writing, on a government form, signed by the company.
slots.felt: Her hair changed. It went dry and flat and the gray came in wiry, so she stopped buying the drugstore bottle and started paying thirty-eight dollars at the salon because the stylist said the cheap stuff was the problem. She has been buying safety. That is what the price tag was for.

slots.title: Is Roundup Safe to Use Around Your House? (2026)
slots.why: Bayer, which owns Monsanto. Rather than defend the warning label, it has been backing state legislation declaring that a federally approved pesticide label satisfies any duty under state law to warn customers, which takes the failure-to-warn claim off the table before anyone can file it.
slots.felt: There is a jug in her garage she has been dragging out every spring for twenty years to hit the cracks in the driveway and the fence line, in flip flops, bare-handed, on a windy day, because that is how everybody's mother did it.

slots.title: Is The Pink Stuff Safe? (2026)
slots.why: Star Brands Manufacturing Ltd, the maker of Stardrops The Pink Stuff. Their Miracle Wash-Up Spray sits on New York's approved waiver register at 4.5 ppm of 1,4-dioxane against a 1 ppm legal limit, and it is on the final waiver tier, the one running December 31, 2024 through December 30, 2025. Two earlier compliance deadlines had already come and gone and they were still asking for an exemption in the last year the state offered one.
slots.felt: Every woman she knows bought the pink tub because of a video. It got the scorch off the glass oven door and the gray marks off the sink and it felt like a small win in a house that has been quietly getting away from her. Nobody told her it was chemistry. It looked like pink icing in a tub.

slots.title: Is Your Dehumidifier a Fire Risk? (2026)
slots.why: Gree, and specifically the two California executives of its U.S. importer, Gree USA. By September 2012 they had reports and test results showing the dehumidifiers were defective and could catch fire. They kept selling them and said nothing to the safety commission for at least six months. Federal law says report immediately.
slots.felt: She runs a dehumidifier in the basement or the bedroom all night, every night, because the damp makes her joints ache and sets off her sinuses, and because she is trying to keep mold out of a house she has lived in for twenty years. It hums under the floor while she sleeps and she has never once thought about it.

slots.title: Is Your Magnesium Really What the Label Says? (2026)
slots.why: eSupplements, LLC, doing business as Nutricost, which sold Magnesium Glycinate printed "420 MG per serving" on the front of the bottle when, plaintiffs allege, the capsules held far less than that. Not a contaminant. Not an ingredient debate. The number on the front of the bottle.
slots.felt: She started taking magnesium for the 3 a.m. wake-ups, the leg cramps that jerk her out of sleep, and the low hum of anxiety her doctor waved off as just her age. She takes it faithfully every night. It is not working, and she has spent a year assuming the problem is her body.

slots.title: What Is Astaxanthin, and Why Do Fifteen Trials Point the Same Way? (2026)
slots.felt: She keeps seeing the word on labels and has no idea whether it is a real thing or a marketing word somebody made up.
slots.study: International Journal of Molecular Sciences, January 2026. Giuseppina Malcangi and colleagues, University of Bari Aldo Moro. A systematic review of 15 randomised controlled trials.
slots.takeaway: Fifteen separate trials landing in the same place is a real signal. What it changes on a blood test is clear. What it changes in a life is still being worked out.

slots.title: Why Did Clorox Pay a $14 Million Fine? What Its Own Scientists Wrote in 2019 (2026)
slots.why: The Clorox Company. CPSC charged it with knowingly failing to report a hazard it was legally required to report immediately. Its own microbiologists wrote the problem down in early 2019. Consumers did not hear about it until October 2022.
slots.felt: That smell is the one her mother used. It is the smell that meant the floors were done and the house was safe and she had held it together for another week. She bought it on trust, not on research.

slots.title: Why Did Eggs Cost So Much? (2026)
slots.why: Cal-Maine Foods, the largest egg producer in America, along with Hickman's Egg Ranch and Versova. The Justice Department alleges they coordinated their bidding to push up the daily Urner Barry price quotation that sets what grocery stores pay for billions of eggs a year, including flooding the market with bids in the hours right before the quote published and placing bids unlikely to ever become real trades.
slots.felt: She stands in front of the egg case doing math. Eggs were the one cheap protein she could still count on, the thing she made when the week ran long and her knees hurt too much to cook properly. She assumed it was bird flu and she assumed there was nothing to be done about it.

slots.title: Why Does My Window Air Conditioner Smell? The Mold Recall Nobody Told Her About (2026)
slots.why: GD Midea Air-Conditioning Equipment Co. Ltd. of China. It built one unit and sold it under ten different names, so a woman who deliberately avoided the Chinese brand still bought the same machine: Midea, Frigidaire, Danby, Insignia, Keystone, Mr. Cool, Perfect Aire, Comfort Aire, Sea Breeze and LBG Products. CPSC found the design let water pool inside instead of draining, which is what grew the mold.
slots.felt: Every summer she wakes with a sore throat, a stuffy head and that heavy tired that coffee does not fix, and every summer she calls it allergies or getting older. The unit blowing on her while she sleeps has been in that bedroom window since 2020.

slots.title: Why Was The Laundress Recalled Twice? (2026)
slots.why: Conopco Inc., doing business as Unilever, maker of The Laundress. The brand was built on being the careful, gentle, premium choice and sold through Target, Nordstrom, Saks Fifth Avenue and Bloomingdale's, and it had to recall the same product line twice inside four months.
slots.felt: She paid four times the drugstore price for the pretty glass bottle because her skin got reactive somewhere around 48 and she decided the good sheets and her own body were worth the upgrade. She bought careful. Careful is what she thought she was paying for.

slots.title: Is Your Skin a Barrier or an Ecosystem? (2026)
slots.felt: Her skin has changed and nothing she used to use works any more. She has been buying stronger and stronger products and getting worse results.
slots.study: Cosmetics, February 2026. Joie Chia and colleagues, University of Sunderland.
slots.takeaway: If skin is a population rather than a surface, then stripping it harder is the opposite of caring for it.

slots.title: Should You Check the Air Before You Go Out Walking? (2026)

slots.felt: She walks most days because it is the one thing she does for herself, and it has never occurred to her that some days it costs more than it gives.
slots.study: State of the Air 2026, April 2026. American Lung Association.
slots.takeaway: A few seconds checking the forecast can spare your lungs an unnecessary hit on the days it is worst.

slots.title: Why Does Everyone Feel Behind on Money at 50? (2026)
slots.felt: She thinks she is the only one who did not work it out, and the shame of that is what stops her asking anybody anything.
slots.study: The 2026 TIAA Institute-GFLEC Personal Finance Index, May 2026. Paul J. Yakoboski and colleagues at the TIAA Institute and Stanford's Global Financial Literacy Excellence Center. Plus the PwC 2026 Employee Financial Wellness Survey, April 2026.
slots.takeaway: More than half the country got the same questions wrong. Feeling behind is not a private failure, and it is not something to be quiet about.

slots.title: Why Can You Not Read a Whole Page Anymore? (2026)
slots.felt: She used to read books. Now she picks one up and gets to the end of a page having taken in none of it, and she has decided that is her age.
slots.study: European Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, June 2026. Marlene Ebster and colleagues, University of Bayreuth. A systematic review of 42 studies covering more than 46,000 young people.
slots.takeaway: It is not your age and it is not your memory. It is a habit that was designed, and a designed habit can be undone.
